title: Summary Of The Question And Answer The Risale I Nurs Duty Of Universal Repair

questions.question: What is this passage mostly about?
questions.answer: It explains why the Risale-i Nur works so hard to help and protect faith.

questions.question: At the start, what kind of talk is described?
questions.answer: An imagined question-and-answer talk.

questions.question: What did the questioner wonder about?
questions.answer: Why more effort was needed when even a small part of the book could answer deniers.

questions.question: What two big things is the Risale-i Nur working for?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and showing His oneness.

questions.question: What picture is used to show that the problem is very big?
questions.answer: A huge fortress that has been damaged.

questions.question: What does the passage say it is not only fixing?
questions.answer: It is not only fixing a small hurt or helping just one person.

questions.question: Besides one person’s heart, what else needs healing?
questions.answer: The shared heart, ideas, and conscience of many people.

questions.question: What harmed these shared beliefs and feelings?
questions.answer: Strong tools of corruption prepared over a very long time.

questions.question: What are the healing things used by the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: The Qur’an, belief, and the Qur’an’s miracle.

questions.question: Why are very strong proofs needed?
questions.answer: Because the damage and wounds are very large.

questions.question: What comparison shows how strong the proofs must be?
questions.answer: They must be as strong as mountains.

questions.question: What else does the Risale-i Nur do besides healing damage?
questions.answer: It helps people move higher and higher in belief.

questions.question: Who is speaking in the first part of the passage?
questions.answer: A person asking why so much more effort is being made.

questions.question: What did that person say a tiny part of the Risale-i Nur could do?
questions.answer: It could quiet even a very stubborn unbeliever.

questions.question: Why did the answer say more work was still needed?
questions.answer: Because the trouble is huge and affects many people, not just one.

questions.question: What building image is used for Islam?
questions.answer: A giant strong fort.

questions.question: How big are the stones in that image?
questions.answer: They are pictured as being as big as mountains.

questions.question: What does this image help us understand?
questions.answer: It helps us see that the religion and its damage are very great.

questions.question: What kind of heart is mentioned besides a private heart?
questions.answer: A shared heart of the community.

questions.question: What happened to people’s common ideas and conscience?
questions.answer: They were broken and were in danger of being spoiled.

questions.question: How long had harmful forces been getting ready?
questions.answer: For about a thousand years.

questions.question: What kind of medicine is mentioned?
questions.answer: Healing from the Qur’an and belief.

questions.question: From where does the passage say the Risale-i Nur comes out?
questions.answer: From the miraculous nature of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What can happen to a person’s iman through the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It can grow and rise through many levels.

questions.question: Why is the Risale-i Nur’s effort described as strong and active?
questions.answer: Because it is dealing with very serious harm to faith.

questions.question: What question is being answered in the passage?
questions.answer: Why so much preparation is needed for defending belief.

questions.question: What is one small thing the Risale-i Nur is not limited to?
questions.answer: It is not limited to fixing a little damage.

questions.question: What is one big thing it is compared to repairing?
questions.answer: A wide fort that stands for Islam.

questions.question: Is the work only for one person’s inner life or for many people too?
questions.answer: It is for many people too.

questions.question: Which three parts of many people are said to need help?
questions.answer: Their shared heart, shared ideas, and shared conscience.

questions.question: What caused these deep hurts?
questions.answer: Corrupting forces built up over a long time.

questions.question: What happened to the foundations and signs of Islam?
questions.answer: They were being destroyed.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention refuge for believers?
questions.answer: To show that Islam’s foundations protect people, especially many believers.

questions.question: What kind of remedies are needed for such big wounds?
questions.answer: Very certain proofs and very powerful cures.

questions.question: Why are many medicines mentioned instead of just one?
questions.answer: Because the sickness is large and has many parts.

questions.question: What feeling did the speaker have after hearing the long discussion?
questions.answer: Great thankfulness.

questions.question: What subject is named in the title of this passage?
questions.answer: The purpose of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How is the conversation introduced?
questions.answer: As a made-up exchange the speaker listened to.

questions.question: What was growing stronger and stronger?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur’s readiness to serve belief and Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What was the main “why” question asked?
questions.answer: Why there was such intense extra work.

questions.question: What answer shows the work is much bigger than a small repair?
questions.answer: It says the work is like fixing huge destruction in a great fort.

questions.question: What does the passage say is inside that great fort?
questions.answer: Islam.

questions.question: What does the passage say is not the only target of reform?
questions.answer: One person’s heart and conscience.

questions.question: What broader problem is being treated?
questions.answer: Damage to the wider community’s thinking and conscience.

questions.question: What tools are used against that damage?
questions.answer: Corrupting means that had been prepared for a very long time.

questions.question: What source gives the Risale-i Nur its healing power?
questions.answer: The miraculous Qur’an.

questions.question: What two helpful things are especially needed for huge wounds?
questions.answer: Strong proofs and effective cures.

questions.question: What final benefit of the Risale-i Nur is named?
questions.answer: It helps believers keep growing in faith.

questions.question: What form does this passage mostly use to teach its message?
questions.answer: A question followed by an answer.

questions.question: What had impressed the questioner about the Risale-i Nur already?
questions.answer: Even a very small piece of it was very powerful.

questions.question: Why might someone think no more effort was needed?
questions.answer: Because such a small part already answered unbelief strongly.

questions.question: Why does the answer disagree with that idea?
questions.answer: Because the problem is not small at all.

questions.question: What is one word that shows the damage is spread very widely?
questions.answer: Vast.

questions.question: What large symbol stands for the religion needing repair?
questions.answer: A fortress.

questions.question: What human qualities are said to be in danger among many people?
questions.answer: Their thinking and their sense of right and wrong.

questions.question: What made the danger especially serious?
questions.answer: It had been built up for a very long time.

questions.question: Who especially needs this refuge and protection?
questions.answer: All people, especially the many believers.

questions.question: What does “proofs of the utmost certitude” mean in simple words?
questions.answer: Very strong proofs people can trust.

questions.question: What does the passage compare the needed cures to?
questions.answer: Many medicines with great power to heal.

questions.question: If a student asked, “Is this only about stopping wrong ideas?” what would the passage also add?
questions.answer: It is also about helping faith grow higher.

questions.question: What is the big job of the Risale-i Nur in this passage?
questions.answer: To repair major harm done to faith and Islam.

questions.question: What did the speaker hear before giving the summary?
questions.answer: A long back-and-forth discussion.

questions.question: What was one reason the questioner was surprised?
questions.answer: A tiny portion of the work already seemed enough to answer very stubborn denial.

questions.question: What does the answer teach about the size of the mission?
questions.answer: It is enormous, not small.

questions.question: What comparison is made between a little home and the real job?
questions.answer: The real job is far bigger than fixing a little home.

questions.question: What does the passage say has been badly broken in society?
questions.answer: People’s shared heart, thoughts, and conscience.

questions.question: What three religious helps are named for healing this break?
questions.answer: The Qur’an, belief, and the Qur’an’s miraculous quality.

questions.question: What had been attacked or destroyed according to the passage?
questions.answer: The foundations, ways, and signs of Islam.

questions.question: Why are mountain-like strength and complete certainty needed?
questions.answer: Because the breaks and wounds are huge.

questions.question: Where does the Risale-i Nur’s help come from?
questions.answer: From the miracle of the Qur’an’s message.

questions.question: What can believers keep doing with its help?
questions.answer: They can keep moving forward in faith.

questions.question: How did the speaker end the passage after hearing the discussion?
questions.answer: By saying he was very thankful and stopped the talk there.
